title: Lesson 7: Close Read-aloud Culminating Task and Reflecting on Guiding Question
objective: Students will retell important events from the story Summer Sun Risin' and reflect on the unit's guiding question about why authors write about the sun, moon, and stars.

what_is_taught.skill: retell important events from a story
use sentence frames and language structures to support oral responses
reflect on learning using the Sit, Kneel, Stand protocol
listen and explain classmates' ideas in own words

what_is_NOT_taught: formal grammar instruction beyond noun, verb, pronoun identification

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify nouns, verbs, and pronouns in a song and story
student_actions.oral_production: sing song with motions, answer questions orally, participate in partner and whole group discussions, share reflections orally
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain classmates' ideas in own words and give examples during discussion
student_actions.comprehension_response: retell important story events orally and respond to guiding questions orally and in discussion contexts, reflect on learning progress orally and through group protocol responses, participate in Turn and Talk and Think-Pair-Share activities to respond to questions about story and song content, and reflect on learning using Sit, Kneel, Stand protocol

evidence.quote: Direct students' attention to the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars'Version 2 song and invite students to join you in singing and doing the motions for the song.
'What nouns are in the song?' (the sun, the moon, the stars, I)
'What verbs are in the song?' (shines, see, lights, make, look)
'What pronouns are in the song?' (it, them)
I can retell important events of what the boy and the sun do throughout Summer Sun Risin'.
Explain that when we retell stories, we tell the important parts again to help us understand the story better and to remember the important parts.

Guide students through the close read-aloud for Summer Sun Risin' using the Close Readaloud Guide: Summer Sun Risin' (Session 5; for teacher reference). Consider using the Reading Literature Checklist (see Assessment Overview and Resources).

Offer students specific feedback on the close reading skills they used as they answered the focus question: What is the boy doing when the sun is rising, at its highest, and setting in the sky? (Example: 'Everyone looked closely at the pictures in the text and listened to the text read aloud to notice and describe all the things the boy does as the sun is changing from sunrise to sunset.')
For ELLs: Underline the prefix re-

Remind students that they have been working toward answering this question through their close reading of Summer Sun Risin'. Tell them they will now add their new learning to the Unit 1 Guiding Question anchor chart.
Invite students to Think-Pair-Share with an elbow partner:
Gather students back together and invite a few students to share with the whole group.
'Can you give an example?' (Responses will vary.)
'Who can tell us what your classmate said in your own words?' (Responses will vary.)

Remind them that the best learning happens when learners check to see how well they are doing and what they can do to be even better. Tell them that this is called assessing and that today they will do use the Sit, Kneel, Stand protocol. Remind students that they used this
Guide students through the protocol using the learning target.
'Who can tell us what your classmate said in your own words?' (Responses will vary.)

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model retelling the story and explain the meaning of retell; model identifying nouns, verbs, and pronouns in the song; model use of protocols such as Think-Pair-Share and Sit, Kneel, Stand.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What nouns are in the song?
What verbs are in the song?
What pronouns are in the song?
If remeans again, what do you think it means to retell?
Was it about the sun or the moon?
Why do you think the author wrote the book?
Who can tell us what your classmate said in your own words?

scope.breadth: story retelling, parts of speech identification, discussion protocols
scope.depth: focus on retelling key story events and identifying nouns, verbs, pronouns in a song

sections_covered.warm_up: Song and Movement: 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' Song
sections_covered.direct_instruction: Close Read-aloud Culminating Task: Summer Sun Risin'
sections_covered.guided_practice: Structured Discussion: Reflecting on Unit 1 Guiding Question

supports.english_language_learners: Encourage ELLs to sing along or sing duets with confident students; underline prefix re- and explain meaning; provide sentence frames for partner talk.
supports.universal_design_udl: Provide alternative seating options; create class songbook with lyrics and motions; scribe student reflections on chart paper.
supports.below_level_reinforce: Use sentence frames and partner talk to scaffold responses.
supports.above_level_extend: Encourage students to generate new lines for the song with matching nouns, verbs, and pronouns.

assessment.method: Oral retelling and participation in discussion protocols; reflection using Sit, Kneel, Stand protocol
